title: Lesson 43 - What a Segment Is: Audiences from the Unified Profile and Batch vs Streaming Decisions
description: Define basic concepts of segmentation and use cases, starting with what a segment is, how it relates to the unified profile, and when batch or streaming style segmentation fits.

questions.question: A consultant must explain what a Data 360 segment actually evaluates when it runs. Which statement is correct?
options: A segment filters raw source rows from the original systems
A segment filters a data model object such as Unified Individual, so it counts one member per unified profile
A segment joins data lake objects directly with no model mapping
A segment only reads calculated insights, never attributes
questions.explanation: Segments run on mapped data model objects and count one member per unified profile, not one per source row, and they read attributes as well as insights.

questions.question: A team wants an audience they can schedule and publish to a marketing destination. Which choice fits?
questions.explanation: Only a standard segment persists membership and can be scheduled and published; dynamic segments are API only, real-time segments cannot be manually published, and a calculated insight is a metric not an audience.

questions.question: Segment membership counts keep coming in lower than the business expects. Which factor best explains the gap?
options: The lookback window limits the data range, and container criteria can narrow it further
Segment membership objects are only written monthly
The segment was built on a custom data model object
questions.explanation: The lookback window bounds the data considered and a container window narrower than the segment level window takes precedence, shrinking the range; a paused target does not change segment membership.
